video_title: This Week Flipped The AI Trade On Its Head
gist: Dan Nathan and Guy Adami dissect the post-midterm two-day reversal in which consumer and rate-sensitive names rallied while AI-centric names crashed (SOXX -12%, Nvidia -9.5%, S&P -4.3% in one day), arguing the AI trade's structure may be unraveling with contagion via neoclouds (CoreWeave CDS), private credit, banks and the mega-IPO pipeline, set against a hot 165k jobs print. A second segment with Peak Six founders Jenny Just and Matt Hulseizer covers prediction markets, 24/7 trading, fractional options and stock-reward loyalty.

insights.claim: The day after the November 2026 midterms, the market rallied broadly but AI-centric names lagged; the next day (Thursday) AI-centric names led a sell-off the hosts describe as the most aggressive leadership reversal outside of pandemics, financial crises or the dot-com bust.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Leadership rotation away from AI was abrupt and election-catalyzed, not gradual.
insights.quote: what happened over the last couple days is probably more aggressive than I've ever seen in leadership

insights.claim: Bipartisan data-center moratoriums and an election result that investors did not expect (including in Texas) put pressure on the AI data-center build-out thesis.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Political/regulatory risk to data-center construction is now a live input for AI infrastructure valuations.

insights.claim: On Thursday Nvidia fell about 9.5%, the SOXX semiconductor ETF closed down 12%, the S&P 500 fell 4.3% and the Nasdaq 100 fell 6.3%, yet the S&P remained up about 7.5% and the Nasdaq 100 about 6% year to date.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Index-level YTD gains mask a deep drawdown inside AI/semis, which may lull investors.
insights.quote: The socks closed down 12%

insights.claim: The SMH semiconductor ETF topped around $660 in mid-June and traded down to roughly $450, about a 33% decline, which Guy Adami calls a slow-motion bear market that culminated in what he labels an outright market crash on Thursday.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Semis are in a confirmed bear market; Thursday was capitulation-scale.
insights.quote: I rarely use the word, but that was a market crash yesterday

insights.claim: The less Nvidia/TSMC-concentrated SOXX ETF was down about 40% from its high as of Thursday's close versus about 33% for SMH, showing breadth of damage beyond the megacaps.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: The equal-weight-ish semis basket is worse off than cap-weighted gauges suggest.

insights.claim: Tesla and SpaceX each fell about 10% on Thursday after falling 4-5% the day before, so their owner lost roughly half a trillion dollars of market cap after spending about $500 million on the elections, including in Texas.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Political spending backfired; the owner may need to double down into 2028 per a Bloomberg report.
insights.quote: He spent $500 million on elections and he lost probably a half a trillion dollars in market cap

insights.claim: On Wednesday's rally, companies that had gone free-cash-flow negative over recent quarters from AI capex rallied, signaling the market would reward companies for not spending on data-center build-outs.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Capex restraint is now being rewarded; watch for companies to cut AI spend guidance.
insights.quote: if you're not going to have to spend money on the build out of these data centers or whatever, we're okay with it

insights.claim: Guy Adami argues the foundation of the AI trade has been on shaky ground and the key open question is whether the structure of the AI trade itself is unraveling, not just technical damage to the stocks.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: If the structure breaks, knock-on effects across credit, banks and the economy would be dramatic.
insights.quote: is the structure of the trade unraveling before our eyes because if it if it is then the knock-on effect to a lot of things is going to be very dramatic

insights.claim: Pod-shop (multi-manager long/short) liquidations and triple-leveraged ETFs accelerated the two-day downside move in semis and tech.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Forced/mechanical selling amplified moves, which can overshoot fundamentals.

insights.claim: Guy Adami thinks the bullish setup would be for the S&P and Nasdaq to gap lower again to flush holders out and then rally into the weekend, rather than a pre-market relief bounce (Nasdaq futures up ~1.3-1.5%).
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: A gap-up relief rally without a flush is less trustworthy than a washout-and-reversal.
insights.quote: you actually want the NASDAQ and the S&P to open gap lower again, flush some people out

insights.claim: Investors have been conditioned to buy every dip in favorite AI names and have been rewarded each time, but Guy Adami believes structural damage has now been done that makes that playbook riskier.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Buy-the-dip reflex may fail this time.
insights.quote: I think there's been some structural damage done

insights.claim: Agreeing with Morgan Stanley's Mike Wilson that the midterms could be a clearing event, Guy Adami says Thursday's high-volume flush could in hindsight mark capitulation even if the market chops and slightly undercuts the early-November low for a few weeks.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: A potential tradable low may be forming, but expect retests.
insights.quote: yesterday was a flush on big volume

insights.claim: CoreWeave closed at $43.66 on Thursday, near its March 2025 IPO price of $40 after trading as high as about $150, and CDS to insure $10 million of its bonds cost about $1.3 million.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Credit markets are pricing real distress in neoclouds.

insights.claim: Neoclouds are the big story of the sell-off, with credit default swaps blowing out in some of these names.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Neocloud credit is the transmission channel to watch for AI-trade contagion.
insights.quote: The big story I think continues to be these NEO clouds

insights.claim: Micron went from the mid-$200s in December to north of $1,200 by summer amid 'new paradigm'/end-of-cyclicality claims, has since been cut in half, and sits near $700 on the bounce, leaving many late buyers in no man's land.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Memory's 'no longer cyclical' narrative has broken; cyclicality reasserted.
insights.quote: you had a cascade of people telling you how cheap it was and how cyclicality was done and this was a new paradigm

insights.claim: Guy Adami argues Micron's management itself missed the memory boom: had they seen it, they would have bought back stock aggressively and positioned to be less supply constrained.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Even insiders failed to forecast the cycle, undercutting confidence in sustained supercycle claims.

insights.claim: Caterpillar, which had traded as an AI build-out beneficiary 'like they cured cancer', has been cut in half.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Industrial AI-adjacent plays are unwinding alongside semis.

themes.theme: Banks, private credit and the IPO pipeline

insights.claim: JPMorgan rose about 4.25% Wednesday, gapped up another 2% Thursday, then dropped from about $360 to $337 within roughly an hour, signaling correlations spiking toward a 'get me out' liquidation.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Bank-stock volatility is a tell that de-risking is cross-asset, not just tech.

insights.claim: Guy Adami believes banks are much later in the cycle than the consensus midcycle view and may be about to roll over, given their dependence on the IPO calendar and their exposure, including off-balance-sheet, to AI infrastructure financing.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Banks are a levered, cyclical play on the AI trade, not a hedge against it.
insights.quote: I think we're much later cycle

insights.claim: Bank of America topped out about a month after semiconductors topped, and the bank move lower mirrored the semis decline, which Guy Adami says is not a coincidence.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Semis may be a leading indicator for bank stocks.
insights.quote: I don't think that's um coincidence

insights.claim: Alternative managers lending into AI data-center and chip SPVs, such as Apollo, Blackstone, KKR and Blue Owl, have shown astounding relative weakness for over a year, which Dan Nathan says has been under-noticed.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Private-credit exposure to AI SPVs is an underappreciated risk channel.

insights.claim: Bloomberg reported large investors questioning Anthropic's planned $100 billion IPO raise, suggesting it looks more like $80 billion; Dan Nathan says Anthropic is damned if it does and damned if it doesn't launch in this market.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Mega-IPO supply and pricing risk is now a market overhang.

insights.claim: Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs each fell about 6% Thursday, Goldman is down 25% from its July all-time high, and SpaceX closed at $123, below its $135 IPO price, as investors price the risk that mega IPOs go pear-shaped.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Underwriters are being marked down for IPO-pipeline risk.
insights.quote: SpaceX closed at 123 yesterday. it's below its 135 um IPO price

themes.theme: Jobs, Fed and the AI-economy link

insights.claim: October payrolls came in at 165,000 versus an estimate of roughly 70,000, and the 10-year yield moved about 5-6 basis points, sitting near 4.86% pre-market with the dollar around 102 and crude around $91.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Hot labor data complicates any dovish pivot.

insights.claim: A hot October jobs number makes Fed Chair Warsh's inflation-fighting job harder, but if the AI trade is breaking down the economy that looks robust on its back will look very different early next year, so the inflation 'dragon' may already be slain.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Fed tightening risk may be overstated if the AI capex engine stalls.
insights.quote: that dragon might have already been slayed if this AI trade is coming undone

insights.claim: Guy Adami says the Fed is in no man's land - no reason to cut and no compelling reason to raise - and his bond-market concerns from six months ago have not gone away despite the rally since the reversal about a month ago.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Bond-market stress remains a latent risk.
insights.quote: I don't think the problem has been solved by any stretch

insights.claim: The midterm result priced out a constitutional-crisis risk premium and raised hopes the new Congress could end the war faster, sending crude lower and airlines, retailers, homebuilders, banks and private-equity names higher on Wednesday.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Energy relief is a tailwind for consumer and rate-sensitive sectors.

insights.claim: Dan Nathan posits a scenario in which data-center moratoriums cut hyperscaler capex, hyperscalers swing back to positive free cash flow and become defensive with pricing power on existing compute, while component suppliers, storage, box makers and neoclouds keep getting crushed.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Within AI, owners of built compute could outperform suppliers in a capex pullback.

insights.claim: Dan Nathan argues the broader market could detach from the AI trade if lower energy prices and inflation strengthen the consumer, while Guy Adami counters that the AI trade's importance to the economy far outweighs any consumer bounce.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Consumer strength is unlikely to offset an AI-capex unwind per Guy.
insights.quote: the magnitude of the AI trade again in my opinion in terms of what it means to the economy far outweighs what a potential bounce in the consumer can do

themes.theme: Peak Six/Apex on new retail market structure

insights.claim: Apex serves roughly 42 million end clients; the share who are women fell from about 34-36% to the low 30s as big crypto companies came to Apex to offer TradFi products.
insights.speaker: Jenny Just
insights.so_what: Crypto firms are adding traditional brokerage via Apex.

insights.claim: Matt Hulseizer says prediction markets were inevitable and are here to stay, noting Peak Six ran in-house prediction markets with its traders about 15 years ago.
insights.speaker: Matt Hulseizer
insights.so_what: Prediction markets are a durable product category, not a fad.
insights.quote: I think it was inevitable

insights.claim: Because most of the population is prohibited from investing in roughly $2 trillion of pre-IPO value such as Anthropic, people will find workarounds like ETFs or tokens; Matt Hulseizer calls the rules Byzantine and obsolete.
insights.speaker: Matt Hulseizer
insights.so_what: Demand for private-company access will keep driving tokenized/ETF wrappers.
insights.quote: you're talking about $2 trillion of value that people can't invest in

insights.claim: 24/7 equity trading is the path Peak Six's Bruce Markets is on, since crypto and currencies already trade continuously; liquidity is the main hurdle and Jenny Just expects adoption to be more natural than people expect.
insights.speaker: Jenny Just
insights.so_what: Round-the-clock equity trading is coming; liquidity providers are positioning.
insights.quote: I do think it's going to be more natural than people expect it to be

insights.claim: Matt Hulseizer expects a fractional options product soon so holders of odd lots (e.g., 78 shares of Meta worth about $50,000) or employee stock can overwrite or hedge despite the 100-share multiplier.
insights.speaker: Matt Hulseizer
insights.so_what: New retail derivatives products widen the options-user base.

insights.claim: Apex is partnering with companies on stock-reward loyalty programs, and Jenny Just cites data showing about a 40% increase in customers coming back over six months when they own shares.
insights.speaker: Jenny Just
insights.so_what: Equity-based loyalty is becoming technologically and regulatorily feasible.
insights.quote: over six months period, 40% increase in uh coming back if you own shares

insights.claim: A Morgan Stanley study cited by Matt Hulseizer found about 88% of venture money goes to all-male teams, 10% to mixed teams and 2% to all-female teams for effectively the same businesses, because allocators reward exaggeration.
insights.speaker: Matt Hulseizer
insights.so_what: Capital allocation biases reward confidence over substance.
insights.quote: they are rewarding exaggeration
